Two years of related administrative, records, property control, evidence control, law enforcement support, or other directly related experience.
Experience handling property and evidence in a law enforcement or public safety environment.
Experience using a law enforcement Computer Aided Dispatch/Records Management System (CAD/RMS) or other records management database.

Property and Evidence Functions - Receive, identify, classify, process, store, safeguard, release, transport, and dispose of police property and evidence in accordance with established procedures and applicable legal requirements. Maintain inventory control and accurate documentation for all items received, including intake records, storage location, movement, transfer, release, and disposition. Ensure property and evidence items are properly packaged, labeled, and documented. Maintain chain of custody documentation and monitor the movement of items throughout storage, testing, release, and final disposition. Coordinate authorized release, destruction, and disposal of adjudicated, obsolete, and unclaimed property and evidence. Prepare routine correspondence and reports related to property disposition. Respond to inquiries regarding property and evidence procedures and status from authorized department personnel, laboratories, courts, and other agencies. Provide instruction to department personnel on proper packaging, submission, and documentation requirements. (65% time)

Administrative Support Functions - Provide administrative support to department operations, including maintaining records, files, logs, and correspondence; preparing routine reports, forms, and other documents; and supporting records retention practices. Screens telephones on behalf of the Chief of Police and Administrative Operations Manager, receive and direct visitors, route inquiries, and provide general information in accordance with established procedures. Coordinate calendars, meetings, and routine logistics as assigned. Prepare routine administrative or financial transactions using applicable systems. Assist with general office support activities. (30% time)
Other Duties as Assigned - Perform other related duties and special assignments in support of department operations. (5% time)
Valid California driver’s license, if required to transport property or evidence as part of assigned duties.

Ability to organize and prioritize multiple assignments in a busy office environment with deadlines and interruptions.
Knowledge of the reporting requirements and crime categories of the Jeanne Clery Act.
Ability to communicate clearly and effectively verbally and in writing.
Ability to interact professionally and effectively with department personnel, outside agencies, and members of the public.

Ability to work independently within established guidelines and exercise sound judgment in routine matters.
Ability to learn applicable laws, regulations, and departmental procedures related to property and evidence control.
